title: Q2 run-rate & procurement prep - scratchpad
content:
Meeting: Q2 Budget Run-rate Review / Procurement Approvals (prep notes)
Date: 2026-03-15 10:00am PT (finance sync)
Location: Zoom / personal notes
Owner: Sofia Ramirez (prep)

Purpose / Goals
- Surface current run-rate assumptions for Exec + Product leads: headcount, infra, cloud, hosting + Redwood Dedicated cost offsets.
- Get approval path clarity for two procurement items: infra reserved capacity (Dedicated GPUs) and security audit retainer.
- Agree on 30/60/90 actions to hit run-rate reduction targets (-12% by EOY).

Quick headline numbers (rounded) — bring source sheet: Q2-runrate tab
- Monthly cash burn (current): $4.25M/mo
- Annualized run-rate (TTM extrap): ~$51M
- Major cost buckets: payroll 62% (~$2.64M/mo), cloud & infra 18% (~$765k/mo), third-party services 9% (~$382k/mo), G&A 11% (~$468k/mo)
- Forecast delta w/ planned hires (Q2 hiring freeze off): +$420k/mo starting May if we onboard 12 FTEs on schedule

Key assumptions to call out in meeting
- Payroll: offer acceptance rate 85%, ramp schedule 3 months to full cost (onus on recruiting to confirm).
- Cloud spend: conservative estimate assumes 10% savings from Redwood Optimize recommendations if applied across hosted workloads by July. Need engineering confirmation (Priya).
- Dedicated capacity CAPEX vs OPEX trade: procurement item A (reserved GPU commitment) is structured as 12-month reservation, $1.4M total, paid as OPEX monthly OR one-time prepay for 8% discount.

Procurement items (decision required)
1) Dedicated GPU commitment (Infra procurement)
   - Ask: Approve $1.4M 12-month reservation (preferred) OR approve $1.29M prepay (8% discount) if legal sign-off fast enough.
   - Rationale: reduces per-token cost by ~28% on high-throughput customer workloads; enables guaranteed SLAs for early enterprise customers.
   - Risks: cash hit if we prepay; utilization risk if model mix shifts. Contingency: include cliff-protection clause and 3-mo rollback credit in contract.
2) Security audit retainer (Compliance)
   - Ask: Approve $120k annual retainer for 3rd-party audit + continuous security monitoring (SOC-compat readiness).
   - Rationale: required for certain Private deployments and enterprise procurement.

Alternatives & staging recommendations
- Staged approval: greenlight half the GPU commit now ($700k) + optional top-up subject to utilization thresholds (util >70% for 4 consecutive weeks). Minimizes upfront cash.
- Financing option: recommend prepay only if legal can confirm refund/transferability to next fiscal if acquisition / major contract shifts.

Notes for talking to Product / Eng leads (angle: revenue enablement)
- Frame GPU commit as enabling $600k/month of new MRR (enterprise customers) if we meet SLA/throughput targets — need Sean (Product) to validate pipeline mapping.
- If Product cannot commit to revenue conversion assumptions, propose 6-month pilot with auto-escalation.

Data & artifacts to have in meeting
- Live sheet: Q2-burn-and-runrate (linked) — show month-by-month, hiring scenarios, and commitment sensitivity.
- Infra utilization dashboard (DevOps) — 7-day and 30-day trailing utilization by model family.
- Contract redline from Procurement team.

Open questions / things to confirm before meeting (owners)
- Verify infra utilization forecast and model families impacted (Priya) — due 2026-03-12 (P1)
- Confirm recruiting pipeline and start dates for 12 planned hires (Liam) — due 2026-03-13 (P1)
- Ask Legal: prepay refundability and transfer clause feasibility (Maya, Legal) — due 2026-03-14 (P2)
- Ask Sales: map pipeline that justifies revenue uplift from Dedicated SLA (Sean) — due 2026-03-14 (P2)

Draft meeting agenda (15–20 min focused)
1) Quick context & ask (2 min) — Sofia
2) Run-rate snapshot & hiring sensitivity (4 min) — show 3 scenarios (freeze, partial ramp, full ramp)
3) Procurement asks (6 min) — GPU commit decision & security retainer + alternatives
4) Risks & mitigation (3 min)
5) Decisions & owners + next steps (2–3 min)

Decision record template (to capture in meeting) — concise lines to drop into notes
- Decision A (GPU commit): Approve / Defer / Approve partial (amount) — owner: CFO — notes: __________________
- Decision B (Security retainer): Approve / Defer — owner: Head of Security — notes: __________________
- Follow-ups: list owners and deadlines

Post-meeting follow-up checklist (my personal actions)
- If GPU commit approved: confirm payment cadence and trigger procurement PO, attach contract draft to Confluence and assign Legal for sign-off (due +2 business days).
- If partial approval: create utilization-based top-up SOW template and share with Infra PM for metrics gating.
- If deferred: propose 6-week pilot and bring sample pilot SOW to next meeting.
- Update run-rate model with final decision and distribute to Exec.

Notes to self (scratchy)
- Keep ROI calc simple: show 3 items: delta-cost per token, expected customer MRR unlocked, payback months (aim <9).
- Prepare 1-slide on downside: utilization <50% -> salvage options (resell, transfer, pause).
- Don't get stuck on legal wording in meeting — capture as follow-up.

Previous meeting follow-ups (from 2026-02-20) — verify status
- Procurement to get vendor pricing options (Procurement: Maya) — status: vendor A and B priced, waiting on volume discount confirmation (Maya).
- Priya to prototype cost-savings from Optimize on dev cluster and share numbers — status: partial, next data slice due 3/12.
- Liam to freeze hiring for non-critical ICs — status: hiring freeze partial lift approved but need names/dates.

Estimated time to assemble final deck: 2–3 hours (one pager + supporting appendix).

Raw quick calcs (paste into sheet later)
- If monthly infra spend reduces by 28% after commit: infra now $765k -> $551k saving $214k/mo -> $2.57M/year (gross)
- If that enables incremental $600k MRR by quarter: ARR delta $7.2M; payback on $1.4M commit approx 2.8 months (back-of-envelope)

End scratchpad. Will clean and convert to meeting doc once numbers confirmed.

Sofia
